A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching content across extensive renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 reports original synthetic emulation experiments, attention-head sensitivity results, and regression experiments on Ames Housing.

after.justification: v2 Section 6 retains these original experiments, including Figures 4–5 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The weight-encoding prompts, softmax-routing constructions, attention-layer compositions, and Hopfield extension are retained. The new distinction between task-specific and prompt-programmable emulation reorganizes existing constructions rather than establishing a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic residual-function and attention-emulation tasks, synthetic Lasso/ridge/linear regression, and Ames Housing regression. No evaluated dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same separately trained task-specific attention baselines for Lasso, ridge, and linear regression. Newly cited theoretical methods are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The experimental protocols remain unchanged, including MSE evaluation, synthetic sample counts, the Ames Housing 80/20 split, preprocessing, model configurations, optimizers, and training budgets.

E4.justification: Figure 5 and Table 1 retain the same sensitivity analysis using 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 attention heads. No new ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over 10 random-seed runs for head-count sensitivity and five runs for the regression comparisons. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 4–5 and Tables 1–3 retain their results. Examples include head-count MSE decreasing from 3.469 to 0.686 and synthetic ridge baseline/frozen MSE of 0.004/0.071. No result entries or empirical findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal definitions and explicit readouts, and Lemma B.1 introduces an input-independent positive gap gamma in its temperature condition. Theorem B.1 also changes its selector expression and changes A's stated output dimension from 3d+n to d+n, although its proof retains 3d+n. The principal proofs and Hopfield results otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: v1's abstract extends the general emulation guarantee to a single head. v2 instead distinguishes task-specific single-head emulation from general prompt programmability using a frozen two-layer module throughout the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. This materially qualifies the central universality/minimality claim, although broader old wording remains in Appendix A.

C2.justification: v2 removes the substantive limitations concerning prompt-size growth, exact real-valued computation, ignored token discretization/numerical noise, and untested language/vision inputs. Permutation equivariance is retained as Remark 4.1 rather than deleted. The loss of these applicability qualifications substantially changes the limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Linear as a column-wise, bias-free map in Definition 2.2 and explicitly documents output readouts in Section 3. These are additional construction specifications; experimental implementation settings, hardware, preprocessing, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds citations distinguishing trained from hand-engineered ICL, and Remark 4.4 adds focused comparisons with linear/ReLU attention, prompting universality, and Turing-completeness research. Most existing related-work discussion moves intact into Appendix A.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around two emulation modes. Former Section 2.1 becomes a dedicated task-specific section, the main theory becomes the prompt-programmable section, and related work is consolidated into Appendix A. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The same five figures and three tables remain, with unchanged graphical content. Placement, spacing, caption references, and surrounding text flow change; for example, Figures 4–5 share a page in v2, while Tables 2–3 occupy separate pages.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the crucial distinction between task-specific single-head emulation and general two-layer prompt programmability, and improves organization and positioning. However, it removes concrete limitations and introduces a dimension mismatch between Theorem B.1 and its proof; Appendix A also retains broader single-head claims. These competing effects on clarity, qualification, and rigor prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
